So What: Purchase costs grew only 11.83%, slower than sales. Margin improved in 4 of 5 categories (only Category05 fell, 18.78% to 17.65%).
Action: Ask procurement what caused lower cost growth (supplier prices or pricing). The data cannot show the reason. Protect what worked.

Findings: Category03 sales fell 62.22% (37,960.04 to 14,339.47) and profit fell 57.20% (4,985.04 to 2,133.47), while other 4 categories grew (+9% to +46%). All 6 Category03 products declined (-22% to -73%).
So What: It is a whole-category problem, not one product. Lost sales: 23,620.57. Data has no stock, price or promotion info to explain why.
Action: Check stock availability, supplier changes or discontinuation of Category03 in 2022, then decide to revive or phase out.

Insights: Heavy dependence on California and Texas
Findings: California (101,142.72) and Texas (64,057.11) together give 41.15% of sales and 42.48% of profit, out of 23 locations.
So What: Business depends on two states. Six small locations (Oregon, Wisconsin, Washington, Virginia, South Carolina, Berlin) have only 5 records each, so there is too little data to judge them. Oregon’s 8.68% margin is lowest but based on 5 records.
Action: Keep stock priority for California and Texas. Monitor Oregon pricing before deciding. Verify “Berlin” (not a US state) is valid data.

Insights: Wholesaler is growing, Online is flat
Findings: Direct Sales gives 51.85% of sales (margin 17.41%). Wholesaler margin is 17.79%, only 0.4 points higher. Wholesaler sales grew 40% (24,699 to 34,649) and profit 71% (3,892 to 6,665) in 2022, while Online sales stayed flat (67,706 to 66,218) with the lowest margin (16.52%).
So What: Channel margin differences are small. The real trend is growth from Wholesaler and Direct (+19%), not Online.
Action: Explore growing Wholesaler volume and find why Online stalled. Data has no shipping or commission cost, so net profit is unknown.

Findings: Product30 and Product19 together earn 11,833.92 (17.17% of total profit). The bottom 5 by profit (Product25, 09, 35, 07, 15) together earn only 1,074.18.
So What: Four of those five are low-priced items (under $20 per unit), so profit per sale is small. Product35 still has a 25.37% margin. Only Product07 has a low margin (9.91%).
Action: Do not delist based on profit alone. Review margin and volume together. Protect stock for Product30 and Product19.

Insights: High sales but low margin products
Findings: Product44 (16,333.92 sales, 7.41% margin) and Product23 (12,853.56 sales, 5.66% margin) sell well but earn far below the company average margin of 17.17%. Product01 and Product34 also have a 5.66% margin.
So What: At the average margin, Product44 and Product23 would earn about 1,600 and 1,500 more profit.
Action: Review purchase price or selling price of these four products.

Findings: Cash and Online are almost equal. 264 vs 263 sales records, sales 199,517 vs 201,895 (49.7% vs 50.3%). Online led in 2021 (133 vs 129), Cash led in 2022 (135 vs 130).
So What: No payment mode dominates, and the lead changes by only 4 to 5 records, so it is normal fluctuation. Cash margin is slightly higher (17.60% vs 16.73%), but online payment fees are not in the data.
Action: No change needed. If fee data becomes available, compare net margin.

Findings: Peak month was October in 2021 (20,453.90) and November in 2022 (26,421.67). Weakest was May 2021 (7,957.46) and April 2022 (11,326.68). May 2022 was one of the strongest months (22,952.99).
So What: Months behave differently each year, so there is no proven seasonality. Each month has only about 22 records, so single months swing a lot.
Action: Do not set monthly stock targets from 2 years of data. Collect more years before planning seasonal stock.
